claim: SNF2h slides nucleosomes most efficiently as a dimer.
source: The SNF2h remodeler slides nucleosomes most efficiently as a dimer, yet how the two protomers avoid a tug-of-war is unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact from prior work.

claim: SNF2h couples histone octamer deformation to nucleosome sliding.
source: Furthermore, SNF2h couples histone octamer deformation to nucleosome sliding, but the underlying structural basis remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact from prior work.

claim: Cryo-EM structures of SNF2h-nucleosome complexes with ADP-BeFx capture two potential reaction intermediates.
source: Here we present cryo-EM structures of SNF2h-nucleosome complexes with ADP-BeFx that capture two potential reaction intermediates.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In one structure, histone residues near the dyad and in the H2A-H2B acidic patch, distal to the active SNF2h protomer, appear disordered.
source: In one structure, histone residues near the dyad and in the H2A-H2B acidic patch, distal to the active SNF2h protomer, appear disordered.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM density maps shown in Figure 2.

claim: The disordered acidic patch is expected to inhibit the second SNF2h protomer.
source: The disordered acidic patch is expected to inhibit the second SNF2h protomer, while disorder near the dyad is expected to promote DNA translocation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations and prior knowledge about the acidic patch's role.

claim: Disorder near the dyad is expected to promote DNA translocation.
source: The disordered acidic patch is expected to inhibit the second SNF2h protomer, while disorder near the dyad is expected to promote DNA translocation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations and prior knowledge.

claim: One structure shows a 2 bp translocation without octamer deformation.
source: The other structure doesn't show octamer deformation, but surprisingly shows a 2 bp translocation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by cryo-EM data shown in Figure 1 and supplements.

claim: FRET studies indicate that ADP-BeFx predisposes SNF2h-nucleosome complexes for an elemental translocation step.
source: FRET studies indicate that ADP-BeFx predisposes SNF2h-nucleosome complexes for an elemental translocation step.
evidence: This is supported by ensemble and single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and 4.

claim: One SNF2h protomer promotes asymmetric octamer deformation to inhibit the second protomer while stimulating directional DNA translocation.
source: We propose a model for allosteric control through the nucleosome, where one SNF2h protomer promotes asymmetric octamer deformation to inhibit the second protomer, while stimulating directional DNA translocation.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural and biochemical data presented.

claim: The ATPase subunits of the SWI/SNF, ISWI and CHD classes carry out most of the biochemical activities of their parent complexes.
source: The ATPase subunits of the SWI/SNF, ISWI and CHD classes have been shown to carry out most of the biochemical activities of their parent complexes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: SWI/SNF motors can generate products ranging from translationally repositioned to fully evicted histone octamers.
source: For example, SWI/SNF motors can generate products ranging from translationally repositioned to fully evicted histone octamers (nucleosome sliding and disassembly, respectively).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: ISWI and CHD family motors appear to only slide nucleosomes.
source: In contrast, the ISWI and CHD family of motors appear to only slide nucleosomes but differ in how their activity is regulated by the extra-nucleosomal DNA flanking a nucleosome and the N-terminal histone H4 tail (Narlikar et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction with citation.

claim: The human ISWI remodeler, SNF2h, functions most optimally as a dimer.
source: Finally, while the human ISWI remodeler, SNF2h, functions most optimally as a dimer, SWI/SNF and CHD family remodelers are proposed to mainly function as monomeric ATPases (Asturias et al., 2004; Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Leschziner et al., 2007; Qiu et al., 2017; Racki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction with citations.

claim: SWI/SNF and CHD family remodelers are proposed to mainly function as monomeric ATPases.
source: Finally, while the human ISWI remodeler, SNF2h, functions most optimally as a dimer, SWI/SNF and CHD family remodelers are proposed to mainly function as monomeric ATPases (Asturias et al., 2004; Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Leschziner et al., 2007; Qiu et al., 2017; Racki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction with citations.

claim: Recent cryo-EM structures of yeast Chd1 showed some states with two Chd1 molecules bound to a nucleosome.
source: We note that recent cryo-EM structures of yeast Chd1 showed some states with two Chd1 molecules bound to a nucleosome, but the mechanistic significance of this dimeric architecture is not known (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited work.

claim: Binding of ADP-BeFx to SNF2h promotes a restricted conformation of the ATPase active site in a manner that is dependent on the H4 tail.
source: Previous studies have further shown that binding of the ATP analog, ADP-BeFx, promotes a restricted conformation of the ATPase active site in a manner that is dependent on the H4 tail (Racki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: Binding of ADP-BeFx to SNF2h promotes conformational flexibility of buried histone residues.
source: Further, binding of ADP-BeFx to SNF2h promotes conformational flexibility of buried histone residues (Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: Restricting histone flexibility via disulfide bonds inhibits nucleosome sliding.
source: This conformational flexibility is functionally important because restricting the flexibility via disulfide bonds inhibits nucleosome sliding (Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: A 3D reconstruction with a single SNF2h bound to a nucleosome was determined at a resolution of 3.4 Å.
source: Using this dataset we determined a 3D reconstruction with a single SNF2h bound to a nucleosome at a resolution of 3.4 Å (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The majority of particles have SNF2h bound to the flanking DNA at Super Helical Location (SHL) −2.
source: The majority of particles contributed to this reconstruction having SNF2h bound to the flanking DNA at Super Helical Location (SHL) −2, judging from the density of flanking DNA.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density.

claim: The nucleotide binding pocket shows clear density of bound ADP.
source: The nucleotide binding pocket shows clear density of bound ADP (Figure 1D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), but we cannot unambiguously confirm the presence of BeFx.
evidence: This is based on the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The presence of BeFx in the nucleotide binding pocket cannot be unambiguously confirmed.
source: The nucleotide binding pocket shows clear density of bound ADP (Figure 1D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), but we cannot unambiguously confirm the presence of BeFx.
evidence: This is a limitation acknowledged by the authors based on the resolution of the density.

claim: The AutoN, HSS, and other regions of SNF2h are not visible at high resolution, suggesting conformational flexibility.
source: In addition to the ATPase domain, SNF2h has a C-terminal domain termed HAND-SANT-SLIDE (HSS), which binds flanking DNA, and an N-terminal region termed AutoN, which plays an autoihibitory role (Figure 3A) (Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Grüne et al., 2003; Zhou et al., 2016). These regions are not visible at high resolution, suggesting conformational flexibility of these regions in this state.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the absence of density in the cryo-EM map.

claim: Two 3D reconstructions were determined from the scintillator-based camera dataset: one of a nucleosome with doubly bound SNF2h and the other with singly bound SNF2h, both at 8.4 Å resolution.
source: From this dataset we determined two three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions, one of a nucleosome with doubly bound SNF2h and the other with singly bound SNF2h, both at 8.4 Å resolution with most histone helices fully resolved (Figure 2A–B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The density of the SNF2h bound at SHL+2 is weaker than that of SNF2h bound at SHL-2 in the doubly bound structure.
source: The density of the SNF2h bound at SHL+2 is weaker than that of SNF2h bound at SHL-2 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The weaker density of SNF2h at SHL+2 likely suggests that this protomer is conformationally more flexible.
source: This difference likely suggests that the SNF2h bound to the nucleosome at SHL+2 is conformationally more flexible.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the weaker density observed.

claim: The active ISWI protomer initiates translocation from SHL+2 and engages the entry site flanking DNA via its HSS domain.
source: Substantial previous work has suggested that when ISWI enzymes move end-positioned nucleosomes towards the center, the active protomer initiates translocation from SHL+2 and engages the entry site flanking DNA via its HSS domain (See Figure 1C for nomeclature) (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Kagalwala et al., 2004; Leonard and Narlikar, 2015; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from cited prior work.

claim: The increased conformational flexibility of the SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 is consistent with this protomer being the active one.
source: The increased conformational flexibility of the SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 is consistent with this protomer being the active one.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the structural observation to prior knowledge.

claim: In the singly bound structures with SNF2h bound at SHL+2, the disorder is asymmetric.
source: However, we noticed that in the singly bound structures, with SNF2h bound at SHL+2, the disorder is asymmetric providing a chance to use the non-disordered half of the octamer as an internal control for achievable resolution.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density.

claim: The reconstruction from singly bound particles suggests asymmetric deformation of the histone core.
source: With this internal control the reconstruction obtained from the singly bound particles suggests asymmetric deformation of the histone core (Figure 2B–C, compare canonical Face B to disordered Face A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: A given SNF2h protomer causes octamer disorder on only one side of the nucleosome.
source: These results suggested that (i) the less well resolved local regions in the doubly bound structure also likely result from increased local disorder and (ii) a given SNF2h protomer causes octamer disorder on only one side of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of the singly and doubly bound structures.

claim: Two regions of the folded histones show increased disorder: helix α2 in H3 and the H2A/H2B acidic patch.
source: Specifically, two regions of the folded histones show increased disorder (helix α2 in H3 and the H2A/H2B acidic patch, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The region of increased disorder at helix α2 in H3 is proximal to the nucleosomal dyad.
source: The region of increased disorder at helix α2 in H3 is proximal to the nucleosomal dyad.
evidence: This is based on the location of the disordered region in the structure.

claim: The region of increased disorder at helix α2 in H3 interfaces with buried residues in H4 that showed increased dynamics in previous NMR studies.
source: This region also interfaces with buried residues in H4 that showed increased dynamics in our previous NMR studies (Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This connects the current structural observation to prior NMR data.

claim: Histone deformation near the dyad could create a relaxed local environment that facilitates disruption and propagation of DNA around the nucleosome.
source: Histone deformation near the dyad could create a relaxed local environment that facilitates disruption and propagation of DNA around the nucleosome.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural observation.

claim: Asymmetry in histone disruption near the dyad may facilitate directionality in the sliding reaction.
source: Further, asymmetry in this disruption may facilitate directionality in the sliding reaction.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural observation.

claim: Constraining the H3 α2 helix by disulfide cross-linking alters the directionality of nucleosome sliding.
source: Consistent with this possibility, our previous work shows that constraining the H3 α2 helix by disulfide cross-linking alters the directionality of nucleosome sliding (Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: Recent studies have suggested asymmetric rearrangements of helix α2 in H3 at 150 mM NaCl.
source: Additionally, recent studies by others have suggested asymmetric rearrangements of helix α2 in H3 at 150 mM NaCl and have found that the same disulfide crosslinks inhibit thermally driven nucleosome sliding (Bilokapic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited work.

claim: Disulfide crosslinks that constrain H3 α2 inhibit thermally driven nucleosome sliding.
source: Additionally, recent studies by others have suggested asymmetric rearrangements of helix α2 in H3 at 150 mM NaCl and have found that the same disulfide crosslinks inhibit thermally driven nucleosome sliding (Bilokapic et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited work.

claim: SNF2h amplifies intrinsic nucleosome dynamics during the sliding reaction.
source: Based on these comparisons, our findings here suggest that SNF2h amplifies intrinsic nucleosome dynamics during the sliding reaction.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison with prior studies.

claim: Interactions between SNF2h and the acidic patch play a critical role in stimulating nucleosome sliding.
source: Previous work has suggested that interactions between SNF2h and the acidic patch play a critical role in stimulating nucleosome sliding (Dann et al., 2017; Gamarra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: The activity of a SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 requires the acidic patch on the undistorted octamer face (Face B).
source: Interestingly, recent biochemical studies using asymmetric acidic patch mutant nucleosomes indicate that the activity of a SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 (as defined in Figure 1C) requires the acidic patch on the undistorted octamer face (Face B) (Levendosky and Bowman, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited work.

claim: Binding of one SNF2h protomer allosterically deforms the acidic patch required by the second protomer on the other side of the nucleosome.
source: All of these observations raise the intriguing possibility that binding of one SNF2h protomer allosterically deforms the acidic patch that is required by the second protomer on the other side of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural observations and prior biochemical data.

claim: Allosteric deformation of the acidic patch could serve to inhibit the second protomer from initiating sliding in the opposite direction, preventing a tug-of-war.
source: Such an allosteric effect could serve to inhibit the second protomer from initiating sliding in the opposite direction, thus preventing a tug-of-war between the two protomers.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural observations.

claim: In both the 3.9 Å and 6.9 Å reconstructions, 2 bp of DNA is translocated from the exit site.
source: Unexpectedly, in both the 3.9 Å and 6.9 Å reconstructions, we observed that 2 bp of DNA is translocated from the exit site (Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 5A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the cryo-EM data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 5.

claim: The DNA density at the exit side of the nucleosome is intact and fully resolved, suggesting tight association of DNA with the histone octamer.
source: The DNA density at the exit side of the nucleosome is intact and fully resolved, suggesting tight association of DNA with the histone octamer, similar to what is observed in other nucleosome structures (Chua et al., 2016; Farnung et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density.

claim: The phosphate groups in the double stranded DNA backbone are clearly resolved, enabling precise location and counting of every bp.
source: The phosphate groups in the double stranded DNA backbone are clearly resolved, which enabled us to precisely locate and count every bp and to confirm the two extra bp on the exit side of the nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplements 3A–B and 5–6).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 5-6.

claim: Nucleosomes assembled identically but untreated with SNF2h do not display the 2 bp translocation of DNA.
source: We ruled out the possibility that the nucleosome particles were pre-assembled with two bp shifted before forming a complex with SNF2h, by determining a reconstruction of nucleosomes assembled identically but untreated with SNF2h (Figure 1—figure supplement 5C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D). These nucleosomes do not display the 2 bp translocation of DNA from the exit side.
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5C.

claim: No extra DNA density was found in the exit side for the structures obtained at 70 mM KCl.
source: Further, intriguingly, no extra DNA density was found in the exit side for the structures obtained at 70 mM KCl (Figure 1—figure supplement 5D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5D.

claim: The reconstructions obtained using the K2 and scintillator-based cameras at 140 mM and 70 mM KCl respectively represent different states of the SNF2h-nucleosome complex.
source: These comparisons indicate that the reconstructions obtained using the K2 and scintillator-based cameras at 140 mM and 70 mM KCl respectively represent different states of the SNF2h-nucleosome complex.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of the structures obtained under different conditions.

claim: The Chd1 remodeling motor can shift 1–3 bp of nucleosomal DNA inwards from the entry site in the apo and ADP states.
source: Recent studies have shown that the Chd1 remodeling motor can shift 1–3 bp of nucleosomal DNA inwards from the entry site in the apo and ADP states (Winger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited work.

claim: Under 140 mM KCl buffer conditions, a change in FRET was observed in the presence of SNF2h and ADP-BeFx.
source: Under the 140 mM KCl buffer conditions of the EM sample preparation, we observed a change in FRET in the presence of SNF2h and ADP-BeFx (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is based on single-molecule FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D.

claim: The extent of FRET change is consistent with the translocation of 1–2 bp of DNA out of the nucleosome.
source: The extent of FRET change is consistent with the change in FRET that would be expected from the translocation of 1–2 bp of DNA out of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRET data.

claim: The FRET change was not observed in the absence of SNF2h.
source: This FRET change was not observed in the absence of SNF2h (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D.

claim: Ensemble FRET experiments with a different labeling scheme showed a change in FRET consistent with DNA translocation.
source: Complementary ensemble FRET experiments with a different labeling scheme that reports on changes in distance between the DNA at the exit and entry sites of the nucleosome also showed a change in FRET that is consistent with DNA translocation (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: This is based on ensemble FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: The ensemble FRET change was dependent on the presence of SNF2h.
source: The ensemble FRET change was also dependent on the presence of SNF2h.
evidence: This is based on the ensemble FRET experiments.

claim: SNF2h can promote the shifting of ~2 bp of DNA in the absence of ATP hydrolysis, analogous to Chd1.
source: These results indicate that analogous to Chd1, SNF2h can promote the shifting of ~2 bp of DNA in the absence of ATP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the FRET data and comparison to Chd1.

claim: At 70 mM KCl, no significant change in FRET was observed in ensemble FRET experiments.
source: To test this possibility, we repeated the ensemble FRET experiment at 70 mM KCl (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D). Under these conditions we did not observe a significant change in FRET explaining the absence of translocation in the 70 mM KCl reconstructions.
evidence: This is based on ensemble FRET experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: The combination of SNF2h binding and higher salt conditions of 140 mM KCl could increase the lability of histone-DNA contacts and promote translocation of a few bp of DNA.
source: We reasoned that the combination of SNF2h binding and the higher salt conditions of 140 mM KCl could increase the lability of the histone-DNA contacts and promote translocation of a few bp of DNA.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation to explain the salt-dependent translocation.

claim: The structures obtained at 140 mM KCl show a higher proportion of singly bound SNF2h at SHL-2 compared to SHL+2.
source: Unlike the structures at 70 mM KCl, the structures obtained at 140 mM KCl show a higher proportion of singly bound SNF2h at SHL-2 compared to SHL+2.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the particle distribution in the cryo-EM data.

claim: All nucleosomes in the higher salt conditions (140 mM KCl) show the 2 bp DNA translocation in the same direction.
source: Yet all the nucleosomes in the higher salt conditions (140 mM KCl) show the 2 bp DNA translocation in the same direction.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM data.

claim: The SNF2h protomer at SHL+2 is conformationally more flexible than that at SHL-2 in the doubly bound complex obtained at 70 mM KCl.
source: Comparison of the individual protomers in the doubly bound complex obtained at 70 mM KCl indicates that the SNF2h protomer at SHL+2 is conformationally more flexible than that at SHL-2 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The increased dynamics of the SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 makes it more prone to dissociate during cryo-EM grid preparation at 140 mM KCl.
source: We speculate that the increased dynamics of the SNF2h protomer bound at SHL+2 makes it more prone to dissociate during the cryo-EM grid preparation procedure carried out in 140 mM KCl.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation to explain the particle distribution.

claim: The structures captured at 140 mM KCl arise from partial disassembly of a doubly bound translocated complex, in which the protomer bound at SHL+2 has promoted translocation.
source: We therefore interpret the structures captured at 140 mM KCl as arising from partial disassembly of a doubly bound translocated complex, in which the protomer bound at SHL+2 has promoted translocation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations and particle distribution.

claim: The reconstructions obtained at 70 mM KCl represent reaction intermediates poised to translocate by exploiting specific deformations in the octamer conformation.
source: Based on the above comparisons, we conclude that the reconstructions obtained at 70 mM KCl, represent reaction intermediates that are poised to translocate by exploiting specific deformations in the octamer conformation, while the reconstructions obtained at 140 mM KCl represent translocated SNF2h-nucleosome states in which the deformed octamer has relaxed to its canonical conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of the structures obtained under different conditions.

claim: The reconstructions obtained at 140 mM KCl represent translocated SNF2h-nucleosome states in which the deformed octamer has relaxed to its canonical conformation.
source: Based on the above comparisons, we conclude that the reconstructions obtained at 70 mM KCl, represent reaction intermediates that are poised to translocate by exploiting specific deformations in the octamer conformation, while the reconstructions obtained at 140 mM KCl represent translocated SNF2h-nucleosome states in which the deformed octamer has relaxed to its canonical conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison of the structures obtained under different conditions.

claim: The structure implies a large conformational rearrangement in the RecA lobes of SNF2h upon nucleosome binding.
source: Similar to observations for the Swi2/Snf2 ATPase domain and Chd1, our structure implies a large conformational rearrangement in the RecA lobes of SNF2h upon nucleosome binding (Farnung et al., 2017; Hauk et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017; Xia et al., 2016; Yan et al., 2016) (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the nucleosome-bound structure to apo structures.

claim: A large conformational change is implied for the brace helix extending from lobe 2.
source: A large conformational change is also implied for the brace helix extending from lobe 2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, orange helices) (Liu et al., 2017; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the nucleosome-bound structure to apo structures.

claim: Several interactions are observed between RecA lobe two and the H4 tail.
source: We see several interactions between RecA lobe two and the H4 tail (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The basic patch residues (KRHRK) of the H4 tail substantially activate ISWI remodeling.
source: Previous work has shown that the basic patch residues (KRHRK) of the H4 tail substantially activate ISWI remodeling, in part by counteracting the auto-inhibitory AutoN region (Clapier et al., 2002; Clapier et al., 2001; Clapier and Cairns, 2012; Dang et al., 2006; Hamiche et al., 2001; Racki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: In the unbound Myceliophthora thermophila ISWI structure, AutoN forms a structured domain that binds a cleft between the two RecA lobes.
source: The crystal structure of Myceliophthora thermophila ISWI revealed that AutoN forms a structured domain that binds a cleft between the two RecA lobes (lobe 1 and lobe 2) of the ATPase domain (Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: In the 3.4 Å structure, the AutoN domain has moved away from the cleft between RecA lobes and one RecA lobe is flipped over the other to form a new cleft for nucleosome binding.
source: In our 3.4 Å structure we find that the AutoN domain has moved away from this cleft and one RecA lobe is flipped over the other to form a new cleft for nucleosome binding (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Most of AutoN is not resolved, suggesting conformational flexibility in this state.
source: Most of AutoN is not resolved suggesting conformational flexibility in this state.
evidence: This is based on the absence of density for AutoN in the cryo-EM map.

claim: Some residues of the RecA lobes that interacted with AutoN in the unbound structure now engage with nucleosomal DNA and the H4 tail.
source: Some residues of the RecA lobes that were shown to interact with AutoN in the unbound Myceliophthora thermophila ISWI structure now engage with the nucleosomal DNA and the H4 tail (Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the nucleosome-bound structure to the apo structure.

claim: An acidic surface on lobe two directly engages the histone H4 tail basic patch.
source: Among these residues is an acidic surface on lobe two that directly engages the histone H4 tail basic patch (Figure 3C, top left).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The exchange of interactions between AutoN and the H4 tail provides a structural explanation for how the H4 tail relieves autoinhibition by AutoN.
source: This exchange of interactions provides a structural explanation for how the H4 tail relieves autoinhibition by AutoN (Clapier and Cairns, 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations and prior knowledge.

claim: Similar interactions between lobe 2 and the H4 tail were observed in the crystal structure of the isolated ATPase lobe 2 of Myceliophthora thermophila ISWI with an H4 tail peptide.
source: Similar interactions were observed previously in the crystal structure of the isolated ATPase lobe 2 of Myceliophthora thermophila ISWI with an H4 tail peptide (Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as prior findings from cited work.

claim: The structure reveals new interactions between a loop within RecA lobe two and the globular region of histone H3.
source: In addition to the H4 tail, the structure reveals new interactions between a loop within RecA lobe two and the globular region of histone H3 (Figure 3C, top right).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Two residues K440 and K443 are in close proximity to make direct contacts with histone H3.
source: Two residues K440 and K443 are in close proximity to make these direct contacts.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure.

claim: K443 is unique to and conserved across ISWI family members.
source: Of these K443 is unique to and conserved across ISWI family members (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Mutating K440 to alanine resulted in a 4-fold defect in the maximal rates of remodeling.
source: Mutating K440 or K443 to alanine resulted in 4- and 6-fold defects respectively in the maximal rates of remodeling (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is based on remodeling assays shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Mutating K443 to alanine resulted in a 6-fold defect in the maximal rates of remodeling.
source: Mutating K440 or K443 to alanine resulted in 4- and 6-fold defects respectively in the maximal rates of remodeling (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is based on remodeling assays shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: The K443A mutation had a much smaller effect on ATPase activity (≤2 fold), suggesting a role in the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to nucleosome sliding.
source: The K443A mutation had a much smaller effect on ATPase activity (≤2 fold), suggesting a role in the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to nucleosome sliding (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on ATPase assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The interactions with H3 may help stabilize octamer deformation during SNF2h remodeling.
source: Based on these functional effects we speculate that the interactions with H3 may help stabilize octamer deformation during SNF2h remodeling.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural and functional data.

claim: Mutating D442 had a small (2-fold) stimulatory effect on remodeling, suggesting this residue plays a modest autoinhibitory role.
source: Another residue in this loop, D442, is in proximity but not close enough to make a direct contact. Mutating it had a small (2-fold) stimulatory effect on remodeling, suggesting this residue plays a modest autoinhibitory role (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is based on remodeling assays shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Similar functionally important interactions between the H3 alpha one helix and an insertion in RecA lobe two are found in structures of the Chd1-nucleosome complex.
source: While comparable H3 contacts by SWI/SNF motors have not been observed, similar functionally important interactions between the H3 alpha one helix and an insertion in RecA lobe two are found in structures of the Chd1-nucleosome complex (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as findings from cited work.

claim: Several residues of the conserved lobe 1 and lobe two motifs are in proximity to the DNA at the SHL-2 region.
source: In terms of DNA interactions, several residues of the conserved lobe 1 and lobe two motifs are in proximity to the DNA at the SHL-2 region (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the structure shown in Figure 4A.

claim: W581 and N448 are conserved between ISWI and SWI/SNF ATPases.
